section.content: A machine learning device (100) learns control parameters for controlling machining conditions in an electric discharge machine (1). A machine learning device (100) is provided with: a state observation unit (30) for observing a plurality of state variables representing the machining state during electric discharge machining; and a learning unit (40) that learns the control parameter based on the plurality of state variables.
机器学习装置(100)对控制放电加工机(1)中的加工条件的控制参数进行学习。机器学习装置(100)具有：状态观测部(30)，其对表示放电加工中的加工状态的多个状态变量进行观测；以及学习部(40)，其基于多个状态变量而学习控制参数。

Machine learning deviceTechnical Field

The present invention relates to a machine learning device, an electric discharge machine, and a machine learning method for learning control parameters for controlling electric discharge machining.

Background

In order to perform stable machining in an electric discharge machine, there is an adaptive control function that automatically changes machining conditions expressed as physical quantities, such as changing a power supply voltage waveform and a power supply current waveform, and changing an inter-electrode control operation, which is a servo operation. The machining conditions are determined by several to more than ten kinds of machining parameters that can be changed by the user. Parameters for changing the magnitude of a voltage applied to machine a workpiece or the shape of a machining current pulse, parameters for adjusting the relative distance between the workpiece and a machining electrode serving as a tool, and parameters for changing the feed rate of the machining electrode correspond to machining parameters.

The combination of these machining parameters is determined experimentally as a set of appropriate values using a typical machining shape, a material to be machined, and a material of an electrode, and thus a plurality of sets are set in advance in the electric discharge machine and can be selected by a user. However, the shape of the object to be machined by the electric discharge machine is a three-dimensional complex shape, and various materials are present for the material to be machined based on the characteristics of the electric discharge machine that can be machined when energized. Therefore, optimization of machining parameters is required, and for example, patent document 1 discloses that machining parameters are automatically set by using a machining state input by an operator.

Patent document 1: japanese laid-open patent publication No. 2-212041

Disclosure of Invention

However, in the automatic setting described in patent document 1, only a part of the machining parameters that can be set by the user is adjusted based on a single type of machining state. In addition, based on the machining parameters, various control parameters exist in large quantities as their background in order to realize the machining conditions that are finally expressed as physical quantities, and these control parameters are not adjusted.

Therefore, adaptive control of the electric discharge machine is required to be capable of obtaining more appropriate machining conditions as physical quantities.

The present invention has been made in view of the above circumstances, and an object thereof is to obtain a machine learning device capable of automatically learning a more appropriate machining condition in electric discharge machining.

In order to solve the above-described problems and achieve the object, a machine learning device according to the present invention learns control parameters for controlling machining conditions in an electric discharge machine. The machine learning device of the present invention includes: a state observation unit that observes a plurality of state variables indicating a machining state during electric discharge machining; and a learning unit that learns the control parameter based on the plurality of state variables.

ADVANTAGEOUS EFFECTS OF INVENTION

The machine learning device according to the present invention has an effect of automatically learning a more appropriate machining condition in electric discharge machining.

Detailed Description

Hereinafter, a machine learning device, an electric discharge machine, and a machine learning method according to embodiments of the present invention will be described in detail with reference to the drawings. The present invention is not limited to the embodiments.

Embodiment 1.

Fig. 1 is a block diagram showing a configuration of an electric discharge machine 1 according to embodiment 1 of the present invention. The electric discharge machine 1 includes: a machining electrode 2 serving as a machining tool; a drive device 4 for controlling the distance between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3; a machining power supply 5 for generating electric discharge between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3; and a control device 10 that controls the drive device 4 and the machining power supply 5. The workpiece 3 is connected to a machining power supply 5. The driving device 4 can drive either one or both of the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3.

The control device 10 includes: a shaft drive control unit 11 that controls the drive device 4; a machining power supply control unit 12 that controls the machining power supply 5; a machining condition setting unit 15 for setting a machining condition set value; a control parameter storage unit 13 for storing control parameters corresponding to the processing conditions; and an initial parameter setting unit 14 that sets an initial value of the control parameter. The machining condition set value is a set value that specifies a machining condition.

The control parameter is a parameter that defines a relationship between the machining condition set value and the machining condition, and determines the machining condition expressed by a specific physical quantity based on the machining condition set value and the control parameter. Therefore, the machining condition of the machining mode in which machining is performed by generating electric discharge between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3 is determined based on the machining condition set value set by the machining condition setting unit 15 and the control parameter stored in the control parameter storage unit 13. That is, the machining conditions expressed by the physical quantities in the electric discharge machine 1 are controlled by the control parameters. The user can set the machining condition setting values, but cannot set or change the control parameters. The axis drive control unit 11 and the machining power supply control unit 12 issue a command corresponding to the machining mode of the machining condition based on the information given from the machining condition setting unit 15 and the control parameter storage unit 13. As will be described later, the initial value of the control parameter initially set in the control parameter storage unit 13 is set by the initial parameter setting unit 14. When the control parameter is expressed by the correspondence table of the machining condition set value and the machining condition, the initial value of the control parameter becomes the correspondence table of the initial value.

The drive device 4 controls the relative distance and the relative speed between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3 based on the above-described command from the axis drive control unit 11. The machining power supply 5 applies a voltage between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3 based on the above-described command from the machining power supply control unit 12, and controls a current waveform during electric discharge.

The control device 10 further includes an input/output unit 20, a machine learning device 100, a parameter changing unit 50, and a learning result storage unit 80.

The input/output unit 20 is an input/output interface for receiving an input from a user and supporting a confirmation operation by the user by displaying the input/output interface. The input/output unit 20 includes: a machining condition input unit 21 that receives a machining condition set value that a user desires to set by the machining condition setting unit 15; and a display unit 22 for performing a confirmation operation for observing the machining state by a user.

The machine learning device 100 includes a state observation unit 30 and a learning unit 40. The state observation unit 30 includes a shaft drive recognition unit 31, a pulse state recognition unit 32, and a machining state observation unit 33. The learning unit 40 has a report calculation unit 47 and a function update unit 48, and performs optimization by learning control parameters.

The reward calculation unit 47 has: a 1 st report calculation unit 41 that calculates a report relating to voltage control; a 2 nd return calculation unit 43 that calculates a return relating to the pulse control; and a 3 rd reward calculation unit 45 that calculates a reward related to the axis drive control. The function update unit 48 includes: a 1 st function update unit 42 that updates a function related to voltage control; a 2 nd function updating unit 44 that updates a function relating to pulse control; and a 3 rd function updating unit 46 that updates a function related to the shaft drive control.

The parameter changing unit 50 includes: a 1 st control parameter changing unit 51 that changes a control parameter of a machining condition related to voltage control; a 2 nd control parameter changing unit 52 that changes a control parameter of a machining condition related to the pulse control; and a 3 rd control parameter changing unit 53 that changes a control parameter of the machining condition related to the shaft drive control. The parameter changing unit 50 changes the control parameter stored in the control parameter storage unit 13 based on the result learned by the learning unit 40.

The learning result storage unit 80 stores the learning result obtained by the machine learning device 100.

When the electric discharge machine 1 starts electric discharge machining, the shaft drive control unit 11 and the machining power supply control unit 12 instruct the electric discharge machine to generate electric discharge between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3 by the operation of the drive device 4 and the machining power supply 5 based on the machining condition set value output from the machining condition setting unit 15.

While the electric discharge machining is in progress, the drive device 4 searches for an optimum relative distance at which electric discharge occurs while decreasing or increasing the relative distance between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3 in accordance with a command from the axis drive control unit 11. Information on the position of the drive shaft and the operation of the drive shaft at this time is acquired by the shaft drive recognition unit 31 and recorded as a shaft behavior history in the machining state observation unit 33.

In addition, while the electric discharge machining is being performed, the machining power supply 5 applies a voltage between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3 in accordance with a command from the machining power supply control unit 12, and generates a current pulse having a current waveform of a commanded shape, simultaneously with the operation of the drive device 4. The machining power supply control unit 12 controls the voltage of the machining power supply 5 so that a current pulse having a current waveform of a commanded shape is generated at a fixed cycle, based on the machining condition set value from the machining condition setting unit 15. However, it is impossible to reliably pulse the current at a certain cycle in the electric discharge machining based on the physical characteristics. In addition, the shape of the current pulse may be different from the current waveform shown by the theoretical value. The generation cycle and the shape of the current pulse, the magnitude and the application cycle of the applied voltage serving as a pulse generation source, and the information on the voltage waveform indicating the shape of the voltage pulse are acquired by the pulse state recognition unit 32 and recorded in the machining state observation unit 33 as a pulse behavior history.

The machining state observation unit 33 acquires the distribution of voltage values, the generation cycle of the current pulse, and the position information, the velocity information, and the acceleration information of the axis at the time of the current pulse generation in a predetermined period from the pulse behavior history and the axis behavior history. The machining state observation unit 33 gives these pieces of information obtained by the electric discharge machining performed under the currently used control parameter to the learning unit 40 in association with the currently used control parameter set in the control parameter storage unit 13.

Next, the stability or instability of the voltage pulse and the current pulse in the electric discharge machining will be described. Fig. 9 is a diagram illustrating states of voltage pulses and current pulses according to embodiment 1. Fig. 10 is a diagram showing a state in which the voltage pulse and the current pulse according to embodiment 1 are stable. Fig. 11 is a diagram showing a case where the voltage pulse and the current pulse according to embodiment 1 are unstable. In fig. 9 to 11, the upper part shows a voltage waveform, and the lower part shows a current waveform.

When a voltage is applied between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3, dielectric breakdown occurs at an unexpected timing, and a current flows. If an ideal relationship between voltage and current is generated, which enables stable processing, a current pulse close to a rectangular wave having a constant inclination and formed by a transistor circuit or the like is generated. This current pulse is shown as a steady discharge in fig. 9. If the relationship between the ideal voltage and current is not satisfied as described above, the current pulse has an unstable shape different from that of the ideal current waveform shown in fig. 9, or the abnormal discharge shown in fig. 9 is generated as an ineffective current in machining.

In the control of electric discharge machining, as one index for controlling the relative distance between electrodes, an average voltage value at every fixed time when electric discharge occurs is observed and controlled. When the ideal relationship between the voltage and the current is maintained, stable discharge is maintained and continued so that the average voltage value becomes the theoretical value as shown in fig. 10. However, when the unstable discharge or the abnormal discharge shown in fig. 9 is repeated, the average voltage value varies from the theoretical value as shown in fig. 11, and the unstable discharge continues. Since the short-circuit state is established when the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3 are in contact with each other with the gap distance removed, and the open state is established when the distance between the machining electrode 2 and the workpiece 3 is separated to a distance at which electric discharge does not occur, the fluctuation of the average voltage value with respect to the theoretical value does not immediately determine the stability or instability of the discharge pulse. In addition, when the stable current pulse pattern shown in fig. 10 continues to occur under ideal conditions, there is an unexpected time interval called a no-load voltage time until dielectric breakdown occurs, and therefore the period of discharge occurrence is not constant. Therefore, the increase and decrease of the discharge generation period is an index independent of the machining stability.

Fig. 12 is a diagram showing an ideal distribution of average voltage values according to embodiment 1. Fig. 13 is a diagram showing a distribution of average voltage values when the stable discharge is continued according to embodiment 1. Fig. 14 is a diagram showing a distribution of average voltage values when the unstable discharge continues according to embodiment 1. In fig. 12 to 14, the horizontal axis represents the average voltage value per predetermined time when discharge occurs, and the vertical axis represents the number of pulses per predetermined time.

When the ideal relationship between the voltage and the current is maintained, the average voltage value is the number of pulses determined from the theoretical value, as shown in fig. 12. In actual machining, based on physical phenomena, the average voltage value is distributed around a desired voltage value, which is a machining condition indicating a target voltage value, and the number of pulses is also distributed. The desired voltage value need not be theoretical. When the machining is stable and the stable discharge is continued as shown in fig. 10, the fluctuation of the average voltage value is small as shown in fig. 13, and the number of pulses becomes the largest in the desired voltage value. In addition, when the machining is unstable and the discharge is continued unstably as shown in fig. 11, the average voltage value is dispersed around the desired voltage value and largely fluctuates as shown in fig. 14, and the pulse number also fluctuates.

The pulse state recognition unit 32 determines whether the distribution is acceptable or not based on the distribution of the voltage at the time of discharge generation in a fixed period, and determines whether the pulse is stable or unstable. For example, the pulse state recognition unit 32 determines whether the voltage pulse and the current pulse are stable or unstable based on the relationship between the average voltage value, the desired voltage value, and the voltage threshold value obtained from the machining power supply control unit 12. Specifically, the pulse state recognition unit 32 generates an unstable signal of the pulse when the absolute value of the deviation of the average voltage value from the desired voltage value per a predetermined time at the time of discharge generation is larger than the voltage threshold value based on the instruction of the machining power supply control unit 12, and obtains a value obtained by accumulating the number of times of generation of the unstable signal over a predetermined period longer than the predetermined time as the value of the 1 st state. The pulse state recognition unit 32 determines the number of pulses generated in a predetermined period, which is obtained from the instruction of the machining power supply control unit 12, as the value of the 2 nd state. The predetermined period may be an operation time from the end of a retracting operation called a lifting operation to the next lifting operation to the end of the retracting operation for generating discharge. The shaft drive recognition unit 31 obtains the shaft feed amount in the drive device 4, which is obtained from the command of the shaft drive control unit 11, as the value of the 3 rd state. The value of the 3 rd state is set such that the feed amount of the shaft becomes a positive value which increases as the machining direction increases, and the feed amount of the shaft becomes a negative value which increases as the retraction direction increases. The 1 st state value, the 2 nd state value, and the 3 rd state value are state variables indicating the machining state during electric discharge machining, and the machining state observation unit 33 displays the 1 st state value, the 2 nd state value, and the 3 rd state value, which are the plurality of acquired state variables, on the display unit 22 in such a manner that they can be observed visually by a user in the form of a histogram or a histogram in a bar graph. As described above, the state observation unit 30 observes the 1 st state value, the 2 nd state value, and the 3 rd state value, which are the plurality of state variables. The 1 st report calculation unit 41, the 2 nd report calculation unit 43, and the 3 rd report calculation unit 45 of the learning unit 40 calculate reports based on the 1 st state value, the 2 nd state value, and the 3 rd state value acquired by the machining state observation unit 33.

Any learning algorithm may be used for the learning algorithm used in the machine learning device 100 including the state observation unit 30, the learning unit 40, and the parameter change unit 50. Next, the operation of optimizing the control parameters by the machine learning device 100 will be described.

Fig. 15 is a flowchart illustrating an optimization process performed by learning control parameters of the machining conditions related to the voltage control according to embodiment 1. The control parameter of the machining condition related to the voltage control is a variable value for performing the voltage control which is a basis of a desired voltage value set as the machining condition, and thus includes not only the magnitude of the voltage but also the shape of the voltage waveform and a voltage reference value called a reference voltage for detecting the discharge. Further, by optimizing the control parameter of the machining condition related to the voltage control, a process is performed in which the initial notch pattern of the voltage and the desired voltage value set as the control parameter during the no-load voltage period is changed to another notch pattern or the like.

The 1 st report calculation unit 41 that calculates the report relating to the voltage control calculates the amount of change in the report based on the value of the 1 st state and the value of the 2 nd state, which are state variables obtained by the pulse state recognition unit 32. The 1 st report calculation unit 41 is not limited to how the value of the 1 st state and the value of the 2 nd state are used to obtain the change amount of the report if the change amount of the report is calculated so as to increase the report when the value of the 1 st state becomes smaller and the value of the 2 nd state becomes larger. Specifically, the reward is increased when the value of state 1 becomes smaller, and the reward is decreased when the value of state 1 becomes larger. In addition, the reward is increased when the value of the 2 nd state becomes larger, and the reward is decreased when the value of the 2 nd state becomes smaller. Further, the method of calculating the return may be determined so that the return is reduced when the number of unstable pulses is reduced and the number of stable pulses is increased, based on a basic reference for increasing the return when the number of unstable pulses is reduced and the number of stable pulses is increased.

Based on the return calculated by the 1 st return calculation unit 41, the 1 st function update unit 42 updates the action cost function Q, which is a function for determining a control parameter related to voltage control. Based on the updated behavior merit function Q, the 1 st control parameter changing unit 51 changes the control parameter of the processing condition related to the voltage control so that the control parameter is most returned.

Based on the above, optimization of the 6 control parameters of the machining conditions related to the voltage control shown in fig. 3 will be described with reference to fig. 15. Fig. 15 is described with priority being set for the control parameters that are executed and changed in a situation where the electric discharge machine 1 continues to perform electric discharge machining, but 6 types of control parameters may be optimized simultaneously.

Before executing the flowchart of fig. 15, the 1 st reward calculation unit 41 already stores an initial value of the reward related to the voltage control. If the initial value of the reward is a fixed value, it is not limited and may be set to 0. First, information of the machining power supply control unit 12 at the time of machining performed by the current machining conditions and control parameters is observed by the state observation unit 30 (step S101). Specifically, the state observation unit 30 acquires a command from the machining power supply control unit 12 during machining. Then, based on the instruction of the machining power supply control unit 12, the pulse state recognition unit 32 calculates the value of the 1 st state and the value of the 2 nd state (step S102). Next, the state variable obtained by the pulse state recognition unit 32, that is, the 1 st state value and the 2 nd state value are given from the machining state observation unit 33 to the 1 st reward calculation unit 41. Here, the value of the 1 st state and the value of the 2 nd state are associated with the currently used control parameter set in the control parameter storage unit 13, and are given from the machining state observation unit 33 to the 1 st reward calculation unit 41.

Then, the 1 st reward calculation unit 41 compares the value of the given 1 st state with the value of the previous 1 st state (step S103). The 1 st report calculation unit 41 stores the value of the 1 st state given last time, and can compare the value with the value of the 1 st state given this time. When the value of the 1 st state is smaller than the value of the previous 1 st state (step S103: small), the 1 st reward calculation unit 41 increases the reward (step S104). That is, in the case where the value of the 1 st state indicates a more stable state than the previous time, the reward is increased. The increased value of the reward here is a predetermined value. When the value of the 1 st state is the same as the value of the previous 1 st state (step S103: same), the 1 st reward calculation unit 41 does not change the reward (step S105). When the value of the 1 st state is larger than the value of the previous 1 st state (step S103: large), the 1 st reward calculation unit 41 decreases the reward (step S106). That is, in the case where the value of the 1 st state indicates a more unstable state than before, the reward is reduced. The reduction value of the reward here is a predetermined value. In addition, since the value of the 1 st state given last time does not exist when the first step S103 is executed, the process proceeds to step S105.

Next, the 1 st reward calculation unit 41 compares the value of the given 2 nd state with the value of the previous 2 nd state (step S107). The 1 st report calculation unit 41 stores the value of the 2 nd state given last time, and can compare the value with the value of the 2 nd state given this time. In conventional adaptive control, the machining condition set value is controlled according to a rule determined to stabilize machining, but adaptive control for changing a control parameter is not performed. That is, according to the machine learning device 100, even under adaptive control use conditions such as the shape of the workpiece, the electrode material, and the electrode shape, which are difficult to assume in advance, the control parameters can be optimized without limiting the application range of the adaptive control, and the stability of the machining can be improved, and the machining speed and the machining accuracy can be improved.
